criteria.quote: Three Magnemite link up, but intelligence doesn’t triple.
criteria.revision: Make the first line set up the contrast before stating the full answer: “Three Magnemite link together—and their brains become one. So what actually reaches about three times Magnemite’s level?”

criteria.quote: Three Magnemite link up, but intelligence doesn’t triple.
What does Magneton gain when three Magnemite link together?
criteria.revision: Make the open loop a sharper evidence-based contrast: “When three Magnemite link, do they gain three minds—or one brain with about three times the electrical power?”

criteria.quote: The result is a power upgrade with one shared mind.
criteria.revision: Reorder the scenes so each reveal builds: establish the three Magnemite, reveal that their brains become one, then reveal the separate payoff that Magneton has about three times Magnemite’s electrical power. Remove “The result is a power upgrade with one shared mind,” since it only summarizes the previous scenes.

criteria.quote: Then the strange part: those three brains become one.
criteria.revision: Move this reveal later. Begin with the link and electrical-power increase, then use “But the strangest change isn’t the power: those three brains become one.”

Replace the repeated shared-mind summary with a new concrete consequence from the research: after the brain reveal, add “And Magneton has about three times Magnemite’s electrical power,” then end without repeating “one mind.”

criteria.quote: Magneton is a power upgrade with one shared mind, not three separate minds working together.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve both halves with the evidence’s sharper contrast: “Magneton doesn’t become three minds working together: its three brains become one, while its electrical power rises to about three times Magnemite’s.”

criteria.quote: More power, or three separate minds?
criteria.revision: Ask about the genuine interpretive split without treating the documented traits as alternatives: “Would you call Magneton smarter—or simply more powerful, given that its three brains become one while its electrical power is about three times Magnemite’s?”
